title: Compaction, tombstones and the delete that comes back

videos.script: Cassandra never changes a file it has written. {{files}} A write lands in memory, then in a new file, an SSTable. An update is a newer file. Compaction merges them. So a delete cannot erase anything. {{tombstone}} It writes a marker, a tombstone, and you will see one on disk. Then a queue built from deletes. {{queue}} One row left, and every read steps over fifteen hundred tombstones to find it. A tombstone has to live long enough to reach every copy. {{grace}} Ten days, by default. And it must meet a repair before it goes. Then the part this lesson is named for. {{zombie}} A wish list, a node stopped, an item deleted while it was down. The grace period passes, and compaction drops the tombstone. The node comes back with the old row. {{repair}} A repair runs, and the deleted item is back on all three nodes. No error anywhere. Two settings were shortened to make it happen in minutes. The mechanism is the real one. {{rule}}
